text:
Raj Patel: Heads-up — we're seeing a spot churn spike in us-central: ~12% eviction rate over the last 5m and a bunch of 504s from the routing layer. Thinking we should land a short-term policy: region failover + model-variant fallback + customer-tier hedging. Any objections?

Maria Gomez: Can you post the eviction distribution by pool? is it mostly N1 preemptible GPUs or the mixed pool? :thinking_face:

Raj Patel: Mainly mixed-capacity pools with preemptible-backed lanes. Quick read: probe shows evictions concentrated on node-pools named gp-mixed-*-preempt with 60% of evictions, and p95 latency spikes for small requests.

Oliver King: Network flakiness in the same AZ earlier — we saw ARP flaps that correlate with the same timeframe. Might be a networking cause + reclaim. Also noticed kube preemption timestamp alignment.

Lenna Chen: Proposal: soft-hedge routing that does two things for the next 30m: 1) warm up reserved-capacity for tier-1 customers (move N GPUs from reservoir into hot pool), 2) if eviction rate > 8% then fanout to region-failover us-west and eu-central for non-data-residency customers, 3) on fallback allow model-variant degrade to smaller quantized variant to reduce per-request resource usage. Example config snippet: 

```yaml
routing_policy:
  priority_rules:
    - match: customer_tier == "enterprise"
      allocate_from: [reserved-hot, dedicated]
      max_fanout: 2
    - match: customer_tier == "standard"
      allocate_from: [mixed-preempt, reserved-hot]
      fallback_variants: [model-v2-quant, model-v2-4bit]
    - match: customer_tier == "free"
      allocate_from: [mixed-preempt]
      max_fanout: 3
  eviction_threshold_pct: 8
  region_failover: {enable: true, allowed_regions: [us-west, eu-central]}
```

Aaron (oncall): Two notes: 1) prefix/KV caches don't survive cross-region failover — we need to account for cold-cache latency. 2) Rolling warm-up of reserved GPUs must be bounded, we can't burst beyond reserve limits.

Jin Park: For implementation, I'd add circuit-breakers per pool so we stop routing to a pool when transient error_rate > 5% for 1m. Also want a quick toggle in the console to flip the model-variant fallback. Pseudo-rule: 

```text
if pool.eviction_rate > 0.08 for 60s:
  start_fanout(allowed_regions)
  for tier in tiers:
    if tier != enterprise: enable_variant_fallback(tier)
  set_circuit(pool, open=True)
```

Maria Gomez: Ops question — how do we measure quality regression when we fallback to quantized variants? We need a tiny eval against canary prompts before enabling for >50% traffic.

Lenna Chen: Agreed. We'll run an inline eval harness (10 canonical prompts) in the routing path and block auto-fallback if regression > 3% on ROUGE/qual metrics. Also add a manual approval for enterprise.

Raj Patel: Sounds good. Action items: 
- Lenna: prepare the routing policy patch and a console toggle (30m window)
- Jin: add pool-level circuit-breaker and the quick-toggle hook (PR)
- Aaron: coordinate with infra on warm-reserve capacity limits and cold-cache mitigation plan
- Maria: draft the 10-prompt eval set and expected thresholds

sre-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-447 — Spot eviction surge in us-central. Pager duty notified.

Oliver King: I'll monitor ARP/network noisy neighbor and attach netflow logs here: https://go/logs/netflow/2076543219

Raj Patel: Ok let's run the soft-hedge for 30m and reconvene in 40. Please drop short progress updates here. :thumbsup:
